Row 4: Operational Wins, Drags & Earnings Call Q&A Audit
QUALITATIVE & TRANSCRIPT FORENSICS

Operational Wins & Catalysts

  • EDIT-401 Strive Study Green Light: Received Australian HREC ethics approval and completed CTN notification to begin Phase 1/2 clinical testing in Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).
  • 10-Month NHP Durability at AHA: Demonstrated >=90% sustained reduction in LDL-C and ~90% reductions in Lp(a) and ApoB over 10 months in ongoing non-human primate studies.
  • Second BMS IND Accepted: BMS advanced BMS-986527 (allogeneic CD70 CAR-T utilizing Editas Cas12a) into Phase 1 in renal cell carcinoma, triggering cash milestone recognition.
  • Revenue Beat & Burn Discipline: Q3 revenue of $10.37M crushed Street expectations ($4.53M), while operating cash burn moderated to -$21.19M.

Execution Drags & Watch Items

  • Ongoing Net Loss Profile: Quarterly GAAP net loss was -$23.39M, as commercial product revenues remain years away pending clinical validation.
  • Patent Defense Legal Costs: G&A expenses rose +9.4% YoY to $13.48M due to increased intellectual property defense activity for the Cas12a/Cas9 patent estates.
  • Clinical Execution Risk: Strive study Part 1 trial safety and enrollment speed in Australia represent crucial hurdles before 2027 efficacy data.
  • Muted After-Hours Reaction: EDIT shares gained a modest +1.82% to $2.80 in after-hours trading, reflecting cautious biotech sentiment and theta burn.
Top Institutional Analyst Q&A and Conference Call Forensic Exchanges
Gena Wang (Barclays) — EDIT-401 Strive Study Initiation & Dose Escalation Strategy

Question: With HREC approval and CTN clearance in hand in Australia, what are the next gating items to dosing the first patient in the Strive study before year-end, and when will we see the first clinical biomarker data?

Executive Answer: Gilmore O'Neill (CEO): 'We have completed site activation in Australia and screening is actively underway. We remain fully on track to dose our first HeFH patient this year and report initial clinical safety and tolerability metrics in the first quarter of 2027, followed by Part 1 topline efficacy in the second half of 2027.'

Forensic Assessment: FIRST PATIENT DOSING 2026 COMMITTED
Yanan Zhu (Wells Fargo) — AHA 10-Month NHP Durability & Competitive LDL-C Positioning

Question: At AHA, you demonstrated >=90% LDL-C reduction sustained over 10 months in NHPs. How does the upregulation mechanism compare to base editing or PCSK9 knockdown approaches in terms of permanence and off-target safety?

Executive Answer: Dan Ory (CMO): 'Our targeted upregulation approach directly restores LDLR protein expression, tackling the root etiology of HeFH. The 10-month preclinical durability data in NHPs showed clean liver specificity, transient LFT blips with zero histopathology, and no genotoxicity in primary human cells, creating a potentially best-in-class profile.'

Forensic Assessment: BEST-IN-CLASS DURABILITY VALIDATED
Greg Harrison (Bank of America) — BMS Collaboration Pipeline & Milestone Inflows

Question: Can you provide more context on the second IND acceptance for BMS-986527 in renal cell carcinoma? Does this trigger near-term cash milestones and validate Cas12a commercial royalties?

Executive Answer: Gilmore O'Neill (CEO): 'The acceptance of the second IND/CTA for BMS-986527 validates both our Cas12a gene editing platform and our collaboration engine. It triggered a milestone payment recognized this quarter and positions Editas for downstream clinical and commercial milestone payments plus tiered royalties as BMS advances into Phase 1.'
